head: a5cdb0d
evidence: THE DEFECT IS PROVEN AT CORPUS SCALE AND NO FIX WAS SHIPPED, BECAUSE NOTHING IN THIS REPO CAN CURRENTLY VALIDATE ONE. (A) THE CONSTANT CANNOT BE RIGHT, and the number that shows it is the spread. Over all 241 laxity-routed SIDs in SID/, locate_seq_ptr_table returns **114 DISTINCT** values of (lo_base - load_address). The constant LAXITY_SEQ_PTRS_LO_OFFSET = $0A1C matches exactly **3** of them. The player is assembled per song, so a load-relative offset is not a property of the format -- which is precisely what 73780fa established for the sequence pointers, and LAXITY_INSTR_TABLE_OFFSET = $0A6B was left behind with the same shape. (B) THE ERROR IS NOT A NEAR MISS. load + $0A6B lands OUTSIDE the loaded data on 69 of 241 files. On the 180 that have a located seq-ptr, the constant agrees with lo_base + $4F on 3; on the other 177 the median |error| is **1,011 bytes** (min 8, max 2,544). An 8x8 instrument table is 64 bytes, so at 1,011 bytes off it reads entirely unrelated memory. (C) THE DELTA HYPOTHESIS IS PLAUSIBLE AND UNVERIFIED. $0A6B - $0A1C = $4F, and locate_seq_ptr_table's own docstring argues the LAYOUT is uniform and only the OFFSET moves. That predicts instr = lo_base + $4F. I could not confirm it. (D) THE VALIDATOR DOES NOT EXIST. sidm2/table_extraction.find_instrument_table -- the only independent, SEARCH-based instrument locator reachable from the declared paths (via laxity_analyzer.extract_instruments, declared r:) -- returns NOTHING for **180 of the 180** files that have a located seq-ptr. It cannot arbitrate between the constant and the delta, so a three-way comparison came back 0/0/0. Shipping a locate change on an unfalsifiable hypothesis is exactly the 'plausible-looking garbage' this module's own comments warn about. (E) NEITHER OPTION IN THE VERIFY IS SHIPPABLE AS WRITTEN. Option (i) -- 'encode it as a CHECKED constant with a test that fails on violation' -- is explicitly conditioned on 'IF the invariant holds'. It does not: 114 offsets, so the check would fail on 238 of 241 files the moment it landed. Option (ii), locate by signature, is the right general answer and is blocked on (D). (F) WHAT SHIPPED IS THE MEASUREMENT, PINNED. A test in pyscript/test_laxity_parser.py asserts the measured shape -- offsets widely variable, constant agreeing on <10% of located files, the constant landing outside the data on >10 files -- so it FAILS if someone fixes the constant, changes the locate, or lands a validator. The docstring carries every figure above and states plainly that it pins the DEFECT, not a fix.

head: a5cdb0d
evidence:
THE VERIFY SAID 'SETTLING IT NEEDS THE PLAY ROUTINE DISASSEMBLED, NOT ANOTHER HEURISTIC'. Disassembled, and the answer is that the instruction the locate is looking for DOES NOT EXIST on these two builds. (A) EVERY DECODING BUILD READS ITS TEMPO WITH AN `LDA abs,y` IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE SIX TRACK-POINTER SITES. Maze_Mania, right after the last track site at $111B:
        STA abs   $158F
        LDA abs,y $1983      <- tune_tempo
        STA abs   $159A
        JMP       $1022
(B) POGO_STICK_OLYMPICS AND WARRIORS GO STRAIGHT TO THE JUMP:
        STA abs   $1407 / $2407
        JMP       $1013 / $2013
There is no load between the store and the jump. So `_locate_tables`' complaint that 'every indexed-read site is claimed by another table' is literally true and unfixable by better claiming -- THERE WAS NEVER A SEVENTH SITE. (C) THE SITE INVENTORY CONFIRMS IT. Pogo has 30 `$b9` sites; the six-site constant-step group (step 3) is sites[3..8] = $16D2..$16E1, and sites[9]/[10] are $16A6/$16BC -- the PATTERN lo/hi tables, diff $16 = 22, exactly the '$16a6/22' the task says is already fixed. Warriors: step 2, sites[3..8] = $26BD..$26C7, then $268F/$26A6, diff $17 = 23, matching '$268f/23'. The next free site on both is a one-byte-apart pair -- the arpeggio pointer table, which is precisely the wrong answer the error message already names. (D) IT IS NOT A BAKED CONSTANT EITHER, so the obvious next guess is also ruled out. Scanning the whole image for `LDA #imm; STA abs` with imm in 1..8 finds, on Pogo, ONE hit -- $1542 LDA #$01; STA $D019 -- a VIC interrupt-acknowledge, not a tempo. Warriors has three, two of them $D019/$D020 and one init store `LDA #$01; STA $240D` that is unmatched on Pogo, so it cannot be the shared mechanism. (E) WHAT SHIPPED IS THE STRUCTURAL FACT, PINNED. A test in pyscript/test_mattgray_parser.py asserts the byte shape at that call site on all three files: Maze_Mania has $8D ... $B9 (store then tempo load); Pogo and Warriors have $8D ... $4C (store then jump). It fails if a `$b9` ever appears there -- i.e. if the premise goes stale.

notes: WHY partial: the verify's bar is 'both files decode through parse_sid with a tempo in the 2-5 range ... probe/decode both go 11/55 -> 13/55'. They still do not decode. What is delivered is the thing the verify said was PREREQUISITE -- the play routine disassembled, and the reason named: the read site is absent, not misassigned. That converts an open search ("which site is the tempo?") into a different and much narrower question ("what sets the tempo when nothing reads a table?"). AN ERROR I MADE AND THE TEST CAUGHT IMMEDIATELY: my first version indexed the byte dump at `site_offset - load + 2`, treating the site offset as the OPERAND position. It is the OPCODE position, so the window started one byte early and the assertion failed with ['0x19', '0x8d', '0x8f', '0x15'] -- the tail of the previous operand followed by the STA. Fixed to +3 and noted in the code. Worth recording because the same off-by-one would silently shift any future disassembly probe in this module by one byte, which is enough to read an operand as an opcode. DURABLE, DO NOT REDO: (1) the pattern table is CORRECT on both files and is not the problem -- $16a6/22 and $268f/23 reproduce exactly; (2) there is no `LDA abs,y` tempo read in either play routine, so no amount of better site-claiming will find one; (3) it is not a simple `LDA #imm; STA abs` constant either -- the only candidates are VIC register writes; (4) two heuristics have already produced silently wrong tempos here (129 from instr_a0, 21/37 from the arpeggio pointer high byte) and a third is not the answer. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD LOOK AT: the store target. head: a5cdb0d
evidence: AN INDEPENDENT LOCATOR EXISTS, ITS KEY GRADES RELIABLE, AND IT REFUTES BOTH CANDIDATES. This was opened as a PREREQUISITE in record 216, where I refused to ship the delta hypothesis because nothing in the repo could arbitrate between it and the shipped constant. The arbitration now exists and its answer is a third option neither branch of the verify anticipated. (A) THE ORACLE. sidm2.instrument_map, not table_extraction. `onsets_with_registers` -> `key_reliability` -> `locate_instrument_table(data, observed_adsrs)`, which ranks candidate layouts by how many of the ADSR values the player ACTUALLY WROTE each one explains. It is independent of laxity_parser in the way that matters: it never reads a load address or an offset constant, only the bytes and the trace. `key_reliability` is what makes it usable as ground truth rather than another guess -- it grades whether ADSR is a valid key on THIS file before any layout is ranked, and it graded four of six RELIABLE. (B) THE FILE SELECTION IS THE VERIFY'S OWN CONDITION, not a convenient subset. I took the 13 top-level SID/*.sid Laxity files where the constant ($1A6B) and the delta (lo_base + $4F) DISAGREE and both land inside the loaded image -- exactly 'a file where the two disagree'. Ran six; four graded reliable (Chaser, Dreamy, Balance, Beast), two suspect (Cycles, Dreams). (C) THE RESULT, and the second run is the one that carries it. The first pass reported the top-ranked layout matched NEITHER candidate on all six -- but with 40 to 2,148 candidates being ranked, a top pick is a best fit among hundreds and I would not report it as an answer. So I asked the stronger question instead: does either candidate appear in the ranked list AT ALL? The constant $1A6B is ABSENT from every candidate list on all four reliable files -- it does not reach min_hits=2, meaning fewer than TWO of the observed onset ADSR values are found there under any layout. The delta is absent on three of four and ranks 974th with 2 hits on the fourth, which is the noise floor. (D) WHY ABSENCE IS THE STRONG FORM. It needs no ranking to be believed. 'The top candidate is $1B3D' depends on the scoring order being trustworthy across 258 candidates; 'the shipped constant explains fewer than two of the ADSRs the player writes' depends only on the hit count at one address. The first is a hypothesis, the second is a refutation, and only the second is recorded as a finding. (E) WHAT LANDED. The docstring of test_the_instrument_offset_is_the_same_bug... now carries the table, the ABSENT verdicts, and an explicit WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED paragraph. No constant was changed and no fix shipped -- the point of the prerequisite was to learn whether the delta was safe to ship, and the answer is that it is not.

That is a real piece of work and it is the successor task, not this one. This task asked for an arbiter and got one; claiming its top pick is the answer would be exactly the over-reach the ABSENT measurement was designed to avoid. A MEASUREMENT CAVEAT I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN BURYING: `locate_instrument_table`'s min_hits=2 floor is what makes ABSENT meaningful, and it is also what makes it a floor rather than a proof -- an address explaining exactly one ADSR is reported identically to one explaining none. Comparing those two directly would have credited the flag with whatever else moved. So I built a CONTROL: the same corpus, same builder, flag OFF. DMC control 1140 vs flag-on 1140; HardTrack 313 vs 313; and PER-SONG, not merely in total -- 0 of 76 DMC songs and 0 of 33 HardTrack songs differ. evidence: THE 84.6% IS DIAGNOSED TO A ONE-FRAME TRANSIENT, THE FIX TAKES THE FILE TO 100.0%, AND THE CORROBORATION THIS TASK WAS RESTING ON IS REFUTED. Both branches of the verify are met; the second is what is shipped. (A) THE PRIOR CLAIM WAS TRUE AND MISLEADING, and catching that is the substance here. The task's own verify carried a 2026-09-03 note: 'the same flag was exercised on MoN (Cybernoid_II sub0) and removes the leading `off` there too -- ours goes off/LP+BP -> LP/LP+BP.' I reproduced it exactly: with INIT_PASSBAND=1 the artifact bytes change and the mode string goes off/LP+BP -> LP/LP+BP. AND THE SCORE DOES NOT MOVE. 84.6% before, 84.6% after, the same 215 audible mismatched frames, dChg=1 both ways. The flag swapped a wrong `off` for a wrong `LP`. An improvement in how a mismatch is SPELLED is not an improvement, and a mode-string report is not a measurement. (B) THE MECHANISM, named from the trace rather than inferred. passband_trace returns $01 (LP) at frame 0 and $03 (LP+BP) from frame 1 onward -- 1440 of 1500 frames are LP+BP, 60 are LP. The seed was `m._init_fmode = (pbtr[min(_w0, len(pbtr)-1)] & 0x07) << 4`, i.e. FRAME 0 ALONE, so it opened the driver on a value the tune holds for exactly one frame. The original holds LP+BP constant (oChg=0), and our build does not reach LP+BP until its first filter program runs ~215 frames in -- which is why both arms cost the same 15.4%. (C) THE FIX AND ITS MEASURED EFFECT. Seed from the MODAL value over the opening 50 frames instead. Cybernoid_II_sub0_native goes 84.6% -> 100.0%, dChg 1 -> 0, and `passband_check --player mon` reports it PASSING -- the verify's first branch, demonstrated. (D) THE FIX IS PROVED INERT WHERE IT COULD HAVE DONE HARM, read-only and without rebuilding a corpus this task does not own. All 13 files in the DMC + HardTrack INIT_PASSBAND A/B (record 227, earlier this session) seed IDENTICALLY under both rules: 13 SAME, 0 DIFF. So that A/B's result -- 11 up / 2 up / 0 regressions / 0 part-count change -- carries over unmodified rather than needing to be re-run. (E) AND IT IS NOT INERT ON MoN, which is stated because it would otherwise be assumed: 12 of 24 MoN songs seed differently under the two rules. Hawkeye sub2/sub3 read LP+BP+HP at frame 0 where the song holds LP; Ice_Age, M_A_C_C, Sample, Thats_preview, Wizzy, Iets_van_JT, Gaplus_preview and Hawkeye_Proto_1 read `off`. None of this reaches a shipped artifact, because INIT_PASSBAND is OFF BY DEFAULT. (F) MUTATION-CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS with the bytecode trap handled (PATTERNS F13): restoring the frame-0 seed turns the new test RED ('the seed no longer looks like a modal-over-a-run rule'); restoring the fix returns 6 passed. __pycache__ cleared on both legs.

evidence: THE REBUILD NOW WRITES A RUN MARKER, AND THE THING IT RECORDS IS THE PART THE ARTIFACTS STRUCTURALLY CANNOT. (A) THE GAP IS NARROWER THAN THE TITLE SAYS, AND SHARPER. Per-artifact `.prov` sidecars already exist (a1e6f9a) and hardtrack_native was in fact the ONLY corpus with a complete set -- 313 of 313 stamped, measured in record 229. So 'the rebuild left no marker' is not true of the files that EXIST. It is exactly true of the ones that do not: 117 of 150 rips are REFUSED, a refusal writes no artifact, and no artifact means no stamp. From the artifacts alone, 'this song was never in the corpus' and 'this song failed the last rebuild' are indistinguishable. That negative space is what the marker records, and it is precisely why the earlier staleness check had to reconstruct coverage from part-count bursts and commit mtimes. (B) WHAT IT WRITES. out/hardtrack_native/_rebuild.json: start and finish timestamps, commit/tree/flags in the same fields as the artifact sidecars, the --first/--last range, whether the run cleared, how many files it considered, every BUILT song with its part count, and every REFUSED song BY NAME. (C) IT IS NOT A .sf2, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `_provenance()` omits a timestamp on purpose -- same-commit rebuilds must stay byte-identical across every sidecar, and three separate no-regression checks rest on that. A run marker SHOULD carry a time, so it is kept out of the `*.sf2` glob every byte-comparison sweep uses. Pinned by a test, because the reasoning is invisible from the filename. (D) --keep APPENDS RATHER THAN OVERWRITING, which is the one place this could have gone quietly wrong. `--keep` exists so a rebuild can be chunked; a marker that kept only the last chunk would report the corpus covered when files 0..N never ran -- reintroducing, one level up, the same false completeness the artifacts already have. A full run (no --keep) clears and starts a fresh history, because a full rebuild is not a continuation of the chunks it replaces. (E) EXERCISED END-TO-END ON A REAL FULL REBUILD, not just unit-tested: 33 built, 117 refused, of 150. The marker's own part total is 313, which EQUALS the artifact count on disk -- two independent numbers agreeing, and the built+refused sum equals considered. (F) IT ALSO REPAIRED A SPLIT I CAUSED. Testing with 1-song chunks re-stamped 9 parts at eaa9f97, leaving the corpus two-stamped (304 at a5cdb0d + 9 at eaa9f97) -- the exact 'not built together' condition provenance_census exists to expose. The full rebuild restored ONE stamp across all 313. (G) MUTATION-CHECKED: replacing `if keep:` with `if False:` in _write_marker turns test_keep_appends_rather_than_overwriting RED with `[4] != [0, 4]` -- literally the chunk-loss failure -- and restoring returns 9 passed.

But the located reader (`_parse_laxity_real_sequences`) returns BEFORE any guard call -- correctly, since a decode cut at the next pointer cannot run away. So Cycles never meets the guard, and that test proves the dsl claim while proving nothing about the guard tolerating a long file. The verify asked for 'a file that legitimately exceeds its dsl still decodes UNDER THE GUARD', and no such test existed. (B) THE REAL COUNTER-EXAMPLE, found by measuring rather than assuming: 64 files exceed their dsl on a GUARDED path. Stinsens_Last_Night_of_89 is the sharpest -- dsl 65, longest sequence 647 (TEN TIMES the dsl), 1,762 entries in 13,449 bytes, routed through the guarded `Laxity SF2 offset-table parser`, and it decodes with zero refusals. Now pinned. (C) TWO READERS HAD NO GUARD AT ALL. `_parse_sequences` marked SIX paths `structural=False` and made only FOUR guard calls. The unguarded two were the final `indexed sequence table` and -- much worse -- `packed-sequence heuristic`, which is where 277 OF THE 411 .sf2 IN SF2/ + out/ END UP. The single reader of first resort was the one with no impossibility check. (D) IT WAS LATENT, NOT ACTIVE, and saying so is the honest form. Across all 411 files, ZERO emit a total exceeding their own byte count, so nothing on disk was tripping the missing guard -- which is exactly why it stayed invisible while the docstring described the guard as covering the fallbacks. Both are now guarded. (E) THE FIX COSTS THE CORPUS NOTHING, measured before and after: routing is byte-for-byte identical at 277 / 78 / 24 / 22 / 10 across the five readers, and 0 files end with no sequences. A guard that changed no file is the right outcome for a latent hole. (F) MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the indexed reader's guard turns the new invariant test RED with '6 heuristic reader(s) but only 5 guard call(s)'; restoring returns 2 passed. 27 tests in the file (was 25).

Balloon VOICE-1 DEAD bundles 24 / Wave2 19 / Filter4 5 / notes 5745. Whole-trace control bundles 2 / Wave2 2 / notes 424. Identical diversity, on every table. Losing one voice removes rows the other two voices still produce, so the distinct SET is unchanged. A floor cannot separate two numbers that are equal. head: 7e67c33
evidence: THE DIAGNOSIS IS COMPLETE AND THE ACTION IS BLOCKED ON A PATH THIS TASK DOES NOT DECLARE. Every measurement the decision needs is below; what cannot be done is the decision's consequence. (A) THE WARNING IS ACCURATE, and I established that by trying to refute it. The message counts `len(exb) - len(breps)`, which is the TOTAL merge count, while `greedy_cluster` prefers GATED merges (the code's own comment calls them 'an INAUDIBLE bundle merge') and only falls back to ungated ones. So the printed number cannot, on its face, distinguish inaudible merges from audible ones -- and labelling all 464 '(ungated) ... WILL be wrong' looked like it might be a conflation. I instrumented the clustering and counted: 553 merge steps, GATED 0, UNGATED 553, 100%. My hypothesis is refuted; the warning is right. (B) BUT THE MECHANISM IS MORE MUNDANE THAN IT READS, which matters for anyone tempted to 'fix' the gate. BUNDLE_TOL defaults to 0, and the call site is `gate=bgate if BUNDLE_TOL > 0 else None` -- so with the shipped configuration the gate is NEVER PASSED and every merge is ungated BY CONSTRUCTION. The 464 are not 464 pairs individually judged audible; they are 464 merges made with the audibility test switched off. The conclusion (the programs are wrong) stands either way, because ungated is what actually happened. (C) IT IS ONE ARTIFACT, NOT A CLASS. out/mon holds exactly three single-file `_native` builds -- Cybernoid_II_sub0, Hawkeye_sub2, Hawkeye_sub3 -- and rebuilding the two Hawkeye ones prints NO force-merge warning. So retiring is a one-file action and 'make the builder refuse' would be a nine-player behaviour change to catch a single case. head: 7e67c33
evidence: THREE FULL CORPUS BUILDS (~1h50m of building): one serial, two at -j8. The differing set is ONE SONG, it is NOT stable across repeats, and the mechanism is named. (A) THE BYTE-COMPARE. serial 1155 artifacts, j8-run1 1119, j8-run2 1125. Of the artifacts present in both: serial vs j8-run1 -> 0 REAL songs differ; serial vs j8-run2 -> 2; j8-run1 vs j8-run2 -> the same 2. Every difference anywhere is Spacegame_Music_part01/part02. Every OTHER real song is byte-identical across all three builds. (B) NOT STABLE. The whole point of the repeat clause: j8-run1 and j8-run2 disagree with each other on Spacegame_Music, so this is a race, not a deterministic parallel/serial difference. In run1 the song FAILED outright (its pre-existing artifacts survived, which is why run1 matched serial); in run2 it produced different bytes. (C) THE MECHANISM, from the error itself rather than inferred: '[70/88] Spacegame_Music ERROR FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] ... out\dmc\_abl_part01.sf2.staging -> ...'. Spacegame_Music tried to commit a staging file belonging to a DIFFERENT prefix. `commit_parts()` walks a MODULE-GLOBAL `_PENDING` list and publishes every staged pair in it, and `dmc_native_sweep --jobs N` uses a ThreadPoolExecutor -- same process, shared globals. So one worker's commit publishes every other worker's in-flight artifacts and clears the list; the next worker's own commit then finds its file already moved. MON_BUILD_LOCK=1 serialises the shared DRIVER section, which is what it was written for, and does not cover `_PENDING`. (D) THE LEFTOVER EVIDENCE CONFIRMS IT. out/dmc held 40 `_ab*.sf2` files before this task (stale staging debris from earlier runs, and NOT songs -- no `_ab*.sid` exists in the corpus). The serial arm left all 40 untouched. j8-run1 left 4: it swept up other workers' debris, committing `_abg_part02.sf2` into existence and pruning 36 others. A serial build cannot do that because only one song's staging exists at a time. (E) THE FREE CLAUSE, ANSWERED: ZERO run_siddump timeouts in all three builds. 7003e9b's bound (30s + 0.5s per trace-second) was measured on an idle machine and had never been exercised under -j8 spawn pressure; it now has been, twice, and did not fire. (F) SCORES MOVED TOO, and F12 says to compare them independently of the artifacts: serial scored 213 voices (66 freq at 100), j8-run1 210 (63), j8-run2 210 (64). The 3-voice gap is Spacegame_Music's three voices dropping out of the scored set.

The shim's non-legato path takes `ons = list(onsets[v])` from the trace, and its own comment warns 'a voice whose decode count != onset count otherwise went silent' -- so an empty onsets[2] would have explained everything. It is not empty: measure_onsets gives v2 67 onsets, first at frame 325. (D) NOR IS IT THE PART WINDOW BEING TOO EARLY, my second hypothesis. part01's span is 9 s = 450 frames and v2's first onset is at frame 325 (6.5 s), comfortably INSIDE it. Dreaming_2_part01's Wave table has 22 non-zero rows and 16 of them carry the gate bit, including $51 -- the exact byte the original writes. (C) SO THE 100.00% IS NOT INSENSITIVITY, IT IS IRRELEVANCE. The parse level DOES respond: LaxityParser._extract_instruments returns 8 instruments with md5 cab9a978 at $0A6B and 8 with md5 d1b22dd1 at $0500 -- genuinely different bytes off a genuinely different table. The emitted SF2 does not change at all. The instruments that reach the artifact come from somewhere other than this locate, so NO downstream measurement -- frame accuracy, register agreement or audio -- can ever see the offset be wrong. (D) THIS CORROBORATES TWO INDEPENDENT FINDINGS. Record 226's ADSR-keyed oracle found $0A6B ABSENT from every candidate layout on four files whose key it grades reliable, and the extraction stage was already noted as inert on this path. A constant that is both refuted AND unused is dead weight that looks load-bearing. (E) THE ARTIFACT SHIPPED IS A TEST, and it deliberately does NOT do what the verify's first branch suggested. Asserting the locate inside the sweep would guard a value the conversion does not consult -- a green check on an irrelevance. head: 7e67c33
evidence: THE DEFECT IS NOT LATENESS. It is MIS-ORDERED NOTE DURATIONS, and the task's '+2 frames late for the whole span' is the first 42% of the span only, with the rest being cumulative drift from transposed durations. (A) REPRODUCED, inside the part's OWN span (24 s, from its .span sidecar) rather than the 30 s I first used -- at 30 s the onset counts do not even match (253 vs 208) and any order-based alignment would be meaningless. Within the span, voice 1 (0-indexed v0) is count-matched 152 == 152. (B) THE OFFSET IS DISCRETE, NOT DRIFTING: {+1: 1, +2: 95, +7: 40, +17: 16}. Every value is the base +2 plus a whole number of 5-frame ROWS -- +7 is one row, +17 is three. The original's onset gaps are {5: 94, 10: 40, 20: 16, 4: 1}, so 5 frames is the row grid. (C) IT IS PIECEWISE, WITH TWO NAMED TRANSITIONS. +2 holds for onsets 1-64 (0.08-6.38 s); at onset 65 it jumps to +17 and stays there for 16 onsets (6.48-12.48 s); from onset 81 it alternates +7/+2 for the remaining 71. So the whole-span '+2 late' reading covers 64 of 152 onsets. (D) A HYPOTHESIS OF MINE, REFUTED BY ITS OWN NUMBERS. 'lateness = gap - 5' fits the three clusters perfectly in the abstract (5->+2, 10->+7, 20->+17) and matches only 107 of 151 (70.9%) in fact, with the exceptions systematically INVERTED (predicted +17 where actual is +7, predicted +7 where actual is +2). A rule that explains the histogram and not the sequence is not the mechanism. (E) THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, from comparing the gap SEQUENCES rather than their histograms: our build carries the RIGHT MULTISET of durations -- ours {5: 95, 20: 16, 10: 40} against the original's {5: 94, 20: 16, 10: 40, 4: 1} -- and assigns them to the WRONG NOTES. The two sequences differ at 44 of 151 positions: at idx 64 the original has a 5 where we emit a 20 (a 15-frame, three-row jump -- exactly where +2 becomes +17); at idx 80 the original has a 20 where we emit a 10 (recovering ten frames, +17 -> +7); and from idx 83 on we repeatedly TRANSPOSE adjacent 5 and 10 gaps. The 'offset' is the running sum of those swaps. (F) IT IS CONFIRMED DISTINCT FROM Fun_Factory, as the task insisted: that was an isolated voice-1 waveform test-bit blip re-arming _arm_filter -- a single event. This is a duration-assignment ordering defect spanning 44 positions, in the opposite direction, on a different song.

head: 7e67c33
evidence: THE NON-INTRUSIVE GROUND-TRUTH ROUTE EXISTS AND IS MAPPED, BUT NOT YET DECISIVE. The verify allows two sources -- the SF2II editor's row display, or a player disassembly -- and I deliberately took the second. (A) THE DISASSEMBLY EXISTS: drivers/laxity/laxity_player_disassembly_ANNOTATED.asm (and an un-annotated sibling). This is the source the verify names and it is IN THE REPO, so the question does not require seizing the desktop. I did not open SF2II. (B) IT IS MACHINE-GENERATED AND HARDER THAN 'annotated' SUGGESTS: 111 KB on 38 physical lines (essentially unwrapped), with Label_N / DataBlock_N naming and no semantic labels. Reading it is a real RE dive, not a grep. (C) THE MASK CENSUS OVER THE WHOLE PLAYER, which is the useful durable artifact: `and #$1F` 2 hits, `and #$0F` 7, `and #$3F` 1, `and #$80` ZERO, `cmp #$80` 1, `cmp #$7F` 5, `cmp #$A0` 1, plus 12 `bmi` and 13 `bpl`. (D) THE TWO `and #$1F` SITES, located with context: $1136 -- `lda $106,X / and #$1F / tay / lda $184,Y` -- the masked value is used as a TABLE INDEX, not a frame count. $1167 -- `lda $106,X / bpl Label_23 / and #$1F / sta $10C,X / sta $106,X` -- bit 7 is tested by SIGN and, when set, the low five bits are kept and stored to per-voice state. (E) SO THE $1F READING IS SUPPORTED BUT NOT ESTABLISHED. $1167 has the right shape for sequence_translator's `(byte & 0x1F) + 1`, and bit 7 being tested by `bpl`/`bmi` rather than masked is consistent with $80 marking a class of byte rather than being a duration. But $1136 shows `& $1F` is ALSO used as an index elsewhere, so the mask alone does not identify a duration, and I have not traced where $106,X is loaded FROM -- which is the step that would settle whether $1167 handles a raw sequence byte at all. (F) ONE OBSERVATION THAT BEARS ON THE THIRD READING: `and #$80` appears ZERO times in the whole player and `cmp #$80` exactly once. CLAUDE.md's '$80 = GATE_OFF, not a duration at all' would be a natural fit for an explicit compare or mask; the player instead branches on the sign bit. That is suggestive, not conclusive.

I first measured a live-voice floor the way BUNDLE_FLOOR was measured -- 36 voices over 11 drivable files, min 12, median 60, max 1037 -- which suggests a floor of ~5 by exactly the same reasoning. THAT REASONING DOES NOT HOLD HERE. Over 60 randomly-sampled non-Gallefoss SIDs, 15 have a voice at <= 4 distinct bundles. Several read [1,1,1] on ALL THREE voices: SID/LFT/Foerklaedd_Gud_eta.sid, SID/Gray_Matt/Always_on_My_Mind.sid, SID/Gray_Matt/Jukebox_64_Part_2.sid -- rips siddump cannot drive (CLAUDE.md records this for LFT explicitly). SID/Gallefoss_Glenn/Arabical.sid reports {0:1,1:1,2:5} with ZERO note onsets on every voice: nothing was traced, so nothing was measured. An absolute per-voice screen would have flagged ~25% of the corpus and the flags would be dominated by untraceable rips rather than by build defects. (D) AND A SECOND, DIFFERENT FALSE POSITIVE: genuinely quiet voices in files that trace FINE. Action_Biker [44, 9, 1], Deliverance [25, 194, 2], Nodule [48, 37, 2] -- two healthy voices and a third carrying ~nothing. So the population splits three ways and an absolute count cannot tell a lost voice from an unused one from an untraced one. (E) SO THE SHIPPED MEASURE IS COMPARATIVE. voice_collapse_vs(ref, new) reports voices ALIVE in the reference and COLLAPSED in the new trace. That removes causes 2 and 3 BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by tuning -- a voice the composer never wrote is dead on both sides, an undrivable rip is dead on both sides, so neither can appear in the difference. (F) AND THE FLOOR IS A DEFINITION, NOT A THRESHOLD. VOICE_BUNDLE_FLOOR = 1 means 'the voice never changed' -- the exercised() shape already in this module -- not a margin chosen below a measured minimum. That is a stronger footing than BUNDLE_FLOOR = 5 has, and the measurement in (C) is why it had to be. (G) MUTATION-CHECKED, the discipline the verify demanded. Four mutations, each RED for its own test: per-voice sets collapsed into one global set (the bundle_diversity mistake reproduced one layer down); the 'alive in the reference' condition dropped from the comparative form; the siddump_per_frame refusal dropped; the floor raised from 1 to 5. Restore verified BYTE-IDENTICAL and 95 passed after it.

So the voice sounds in six regions on both sides, agrees closely on part14 (75 vs 77), and diverges in two opposite directions: it is MISSING on part01 and roughly DOUBLED on parts 19-22. Part 1 is the one part where our voice 3 is genuinely dead, so a part-1 number generalised to the voice reads as a silent voice. The 'audible 0.0% wf' figure that opened this task is correct AND is a statement about 9 seconds of an 80-second song. (C) PART 01 AND PART 06 LOOK LIKE ONE DISPLACED EVENT: the original sounds 75 frames in part01 (frames 325-400) and nothing in part06; we do the exact opposite (0 in part01, 36 in part06). The original's voice-3 motif recurs in parts 01, 07, 14, 19-22; ours in 06, 07, 14, 19-22 -- the first occurrence is the one that moves, not all of them, so this is not a constant offset. (D) THE WAVE TABLE IS EXONERATED, closing the suspect the previous cycle named. head: 57f6ca3

Each note lands where the original's NEXT note begins. (A) THE DECISIVE TEST is on the gap SEQUENCE, and it is unambiguous: identity gg[i]==og[i] 107/151 (70.9%); shift LEFT by 1 gg[i]==og[i+1] 150/151 (99.3%); shift RIGHT by 1 111/151 (73.5%); shift LEFT by 2 106/151 (70.2%). If gg[i]==og[i+1] then the running offset telescopes to a constant plus og[k]; sweeping C over -10..+10 gives a unique best of C = -3 matching 151/151 with no exceptions. (A) THE PREMISE IS EXACTLY AS STATED, confirmed at bin/build_romuzak_native_song.py:173-181: the loop writes edit[wo + 0*256 + start + r] and edit[wo + 1*256 + start + r] for every row, and only afterwards does wave_cursor += len(wp) and raise on > 256. The out-of-range write is real and is not defended against. (B) LEG 1 -- THE CHECK IS ARITHMETICALLY EQUIVALENT TO A PRE-WRITE CHECK. The highest index written is start + len(wp) - 1 and the cursor tested is start + len(wp), so 'some write used an index >= 256' and 'cursor > 256' are the SAME predicate. It rejects exactly the programs a pre-write check would, one instruction later. Simulated over start 0..299 x length 1..39 rather than argued. (C) LEG 2 -- the spill lands in `edit`, an in-memory buffer, which is discarded when the exception propagates. (D) LEG 3 -- THE RAISE PRECEDES THE layout.inc WRITE. gen_includes_song's docstring says it writes drivers_src/romuzak/layout.inc; that open() is at line 270, the raise at 181. A refused build therefore leaves no half-written layout describing a table that was never laid. (E) LEG 4 -- NOTHING CATCHES IT ON THE EMIT PATH. BM.emit_one at bin/build_dmc_native_song.py:369 is not inside any try. The file does contain a try/except (line 394) and it is tempting to assume that is the guard, but it wraps the post-build SCORING loop and reads artifacts back from disk. head: 57f6ca3
evidence: THE DEFECT IS WORSE THAN THE TASK DESCRIBED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE FIX. The task says serve leaves an orphan and 'nothing says it is running'. Measured, the real fault is that a SECOND serve on an occupied port SUCCEEDS. (A) serve() ALREADY HAD AN ERROR PATH -- `except OSError` printing 'cannot bind ...' and returning 2 -- so the obvious reading, that it lacked one, is wrong. (B) THAT PATH IS EFFECTIVELY DEAD ON WINDOWS. http.server.HTTPServer sets allow_reuse_address = True, and SO_REUSEADDR on Windows permits binding an address ALREADY IN USE. Measured against the live orphan on 8791: the second bind SUCCEEDED. Two servers then hold the port, which one answers any given connection is undefined, and BOTH return 200 -- so a reader can be served a build/listen snapshot from a process they have forgotten about, silently. (C) THE FIX IS A PRE-BIND PROBE, NOT A FLAG FLIP. _port_in_use() connects to the port and serve() refuses BEFORE binding. allow_reuse_address is deliberately left ON: on POSIX it is what lets the server restart immediately after a crash instead of waiting out TIME_WAIT, which is the case this tool is most often restarted in. Turning it off to make bind() fail would fix Windows by regressing the common POSIX path. (D) THE OSError BRANCH IS KEPT, NOT REPLACED -- it still covers a privileged port, a bad interface, and the POSIX in-use error, and a test pins that it still reports. (E) DEMONSTRATED THROUGH THE REAL CLI against the actually-running orphan, not only in tests: `abpage.py serve --port 8791` now prints the refusal, exits 2, names the next port, and the live server still answers 200 afterwards -- it was neither shadowed nor disturbed.

evidence: ANSWERED BOTH WAYS THE VERIFY ALLOWS, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE BIGGER FINDING. (A) THE SPIKE IS REAL, NOT SATURATION. The measure has no ceiling at 6 -- the same corpora produce 6 through 68+. Every 6-bundle artifact has the IDENTICAL shape, 100 of 100 sampled: Wave2 6 distinct, Filter3 0 distinct, Filter4 0 distinct. So a 6 means 'six distinct wave rows and no filter programs at all', which is a genuine property of the artifacts. (B) IT IS ONE BUILDER. Concentrated in SDI (90 of 300 sampled, 30.0%) with a little DMC (10 of 300, 3.3%), and ENTIRELY ABSENT from fc, soundmonitor, mon and hardtrack_native -- 0 of 574, those four scanned in FULL rather than sampled. 30.0% x 5039 + 3.3% x 1177 = 1,551 against the 1,569 actually observed, so the two populations account for the whole spike. (C) THE MEASURE NAMES A TABLE THE FORMAT DOES NOT HAVE. This is what the spike led to and it was not in the task. bundle_diversity sums distinct non-zero rows over _PROGRAM_TABLES = ('Wave', 'Pulse', 'Filter') and its docstring says 'wave/pulse/filter program tables'. Across 210 artifacts spanning all six corpora, NOT ONE per_table ever contains a Pulse entry. It is not a naming mismatch and not a locate failure: the SF2 descriptor set is Instruments, Commands, Wave, Filter(3), Filter(4), Tempo(6), Tempo(7), HR(5), Arpeggio(8) -- there IS no Pulse table. The 'Pulse' term has never contributed anything and never could. (D) SO THE SCREEN IS NARROWER THAN IT READS, and on exactly the population in question it is WAVE-ONLY: both Filter tables are all-zero on every 6, so the entire one-row margin over BUNDLE_FLOOR = 5 rests on the wave table alone. (E) NOTHING ALREADY MEASURED CHANGES. The Pulse term was always zero, so the corpus audit's 6,790/14/0 result stands exactly as recorded -- this corrects what the measure CLAIMS to cover, not any number it produced.

Built total 1070 against the recorded 1092 (150% vs 153%). (B) THE ORIGINAL IS A PERFECTLY REGULAR FIGURE, which is what makes the defect legible. On all four parts voice 3 gates on a UNIFORM 10-frame grid with run lengths of only 2 or 5 frames, in an exact 2:1 ratio: part19 16x2 + 8x5, part20 40x2 + 20x5, part21 35x2 + 15x5, part22 20x2 + 10x5. Every inter-onset gap is exactly 10. (C) OURS IS IRREGULAR AROUND THE SAME MEAN, NOT UNIFORMLY LONGER. Part21 built onsets run 6,14,18,24,34,44,56,64,74, 84,88,94 -- gaps of 8,4,6,10,10,12,8,10,10,4,6 against a uniform 10. Part20 drifts for six runs then LOCKS ON exactly ((66,67),(76,77),(86,90),(96,97),(106,110),(116,117) identical on both sides). So this is boundary RECONSTRUCTION going wrong, not a uniform release tail. (D) THE VERIFY'S OWN GUESS IS REFUTED. It says 'probably release-tail shaped'. evidence: DECIDED AND RECORDED, WHICH IS WHAT THE VERIFY ASKS FOR: the fallback readers are INADEQUATE for this population. Drawing nothing is NOT honest -- the orderlists prove real multi-sequence songs are present and the fallbacks find a minority of them. (A) THE MECHANISM, ON THE NAMED FILE. 2_Young_2_Die_native_part01 is 18,043 bytes. The generic packed-sequence parser decodes 21,068 entries -- impossible, correctly refused. The fallback then produces a POSSIBLE decode: 5 sequences, 2,710 entries, ids {0, 9, 64, 79, 96}. But its orderlist references ids 0-9 (0,1,2 on track 0; 3,4,5,6 on track 1; 7,8,9 on track 2). EIGHT of the ten referenced sequences are absent, and the two that exist are over-read. So all three tracks draw nothing. The fallback did not return fewer rows of the same song -- it returned a DIFFERENT SET OF BODIES. (B) THE SHAPE IS THE POPULATION, not this file. Random sample of the same corpus, 3,561 .sf2 scanned under out/ and SF2/, 120 refused (3.4%, consistent with the recorded 310/8,716): 106 (88%) draw zero rows -- independently reproducing the recorded 282/310 = 91%; 119 (99%) have an orderlist referencing a sequence the fallback never produced; 48 (40%) additionally produce ids nothing references. Across the sample the fallbacks supply 305 sequences against 613 referenced-but-missing -- about ONE THIRD of what is asked for. (C) I TRIED TO FALSIFY IT AND FAILED, which is what makes this a decision rather than an impression. If the ORDERLIST were itself garbage, 'missing' would mean nothing. Tested: 118 of 120 files (98%) have a referenced sequence set that is a CONTIGUOUS RUN starting at 0 or 1; referenced-but-missing ids reach only 26 with 96% at or below 16; produced-but-unreferenced ids reach 126 with only 43% at or below 16. Dense low ids asked for, scattered high ids found. The orderlist is trustworthy; the fallback is locating the wrong bodies. (D) THE GUARD IS NOT AT FAULT AND MUST NOT BE LOOSENED, and I checked its shape before concluding: _refuse_impossible_decode tests the TOTAL entries against the file's byte count and, on refusal, CLEARS every sequence. That looked like the obvious culprit -- one runaway body discarding good siblings -- but it is not what happens here: the fallback that takes over produces a possible decode (2,710 < 18,043) which is simply the wrong one. The loss is decode QUALITY downstream of the refusal, not the refusal's granularity. (E) READERS RESPONSIBLE, measured: on the refused files the fallback that ends up supplying sequences is the 'indexed sequence table' (68 of 120) or the 'packed-sequence heuristic' (52 of 120).

head: 57f6ca3
evidence: THE BYTE RANGE IS SETTLED AGAINST THE PLAYER'S OWN 6502 CODE, AND ALL THREE IN-REPO READINGS ARE WRONG -- each differently. The verify's first clause (establish it, write it into LAXITY.md with the evidence) is complete; the second (make the code agree) was deliberately NOT done, for a measured reason. (A) THE GROUND TRUTH IS THE DISASSEMBLY, exactly as the verify requires -- not another module in this repo, which is what made the three readings unresolvable from the inside. drivers/laxity/laxity_player_disassembly.asm (SIDwinder disassembly of Stinsen's Last Night of '89, a native NP21 rip). The sequence-byte reader: `bpl` skips anything with bit 7 clear; then `cmp #$90 / bcc / inc DataBlock_6+$100,X` bumps a SEPARATE flag when bit 4 is set; then **`and #$0F`** stores the LOW NIBBLE to $FD,X; then `iny / lda (ZP_0),Y` fetches the note. (B) THE +1 IS SETTLED BY THE COUNTER, not assumed. $FD,X is copied verbatim to $EE,X (line 150), and the per-frame path is `dec DataBlock_6+$EE,X / bpl Label_16` -- the row advances only when the counter goes NEGATIVE. So a stored n survives n decrements and advances on the n+1th: **duration = (byte & $0F) + 1 frames, 1..16 for $80..$8F**. (C) SO ALL THREE READINGS ARE WRONG. sequence_translator.py:233's `(b & $1F) + 1` has the RIGHT +1 and the WRONG mask -- $1F folds bit 4 into the count. unpack_sequence's `b & $0F` with bit 4 = tie has the RIGHT mask and the RIGHT bit-4 split but NO +1, so every duration is one frame short. CLAUDE.md's `$80 = GATE_OFF` is wrong for this stream entirely: $80 is a duration byte whose nibble is 0, i.e. one frame. (D) AND THE FLAG IS NOT PURELY A TIE, which no reading captured: the same $100,X location is incremented at line 140 when the NOTE byte is $00 or $7E. It is a shared gate/continue flag that bit 4 is one input to. Calling it `tie` in a decoder happens to work; it is not the player's model. (E) THE MASK DIFFERENCE IS NOT INERT, which is what decided the scope. Over the 6 SID/Laxity/*.sid files whose sequence table locates: **1,708 duration bytes, 232 of them (13.6%) with bit 4 set** -- exactly the population where $1F and $0F disagree. Switching the mask changes roughly one event in seven.

I did not implement it: it is a real design step rather than a knob, and the verify's bar (narrow to one AND re-verify 22 files unmoved) is a full cycle's work on its own. This matters because it removes the obvious explanation ('some other table stole the tempo's operand'). Pogo_Stick_Olympics $16D2 reads `00 31 07 | 00 17 1A | 00 4F 09 | 00 17 1A | 00 82 0B | 00 17 1A` -- stride 3, three subtunes, decoding to per-voice pointers $1731/$174F/$1782 (lo) with hi bytes $17 and $1A. On Pogo the operands cover $1451..$16E3 with only $1511/$1512 free, and those are a legitimate arpeggio POINTER table -- its bytes `23 21 27 21 31 21` are interleaved lo/hi giving $1517/$151B/$151F, and $1517 holds `0 5 9 12` and `0 4 7 12`, which are arpeggio CHORDS (0,4,7,12 is a major triad). Searched as `<load> ; sta abs ; jmp`, that idiom is UNIQUE in every image and its operand equals tune_tempo on 8 of 8 files that locate -- Bangkok_Knights_Loader, Driller, Hyperion_2, KGB_Superspy, Make_My_Day, Maze_Mania, Motocross, THEC64-Hall_of_Fame. The idiom is therefore not 'the tempo read' at all -- it is 'the last load before the routine jumps', which on 8 builds happens to be the tempo and on these two is the track pointer. An 8-of-8 agreement across four different stride layouts still did not make it a rule. (E) A THIRD MECHANISM ELIMINATED: there is no immediate tempo either. Searching all four images for `lda #n ; sta abs` or `lda #n ; sta zp` with n in 1..12 returns NOTHING on any of them, including the two that work -- so 'this build hardcodes its tempo' is refuted rather than merely unproven.

evidence: SOLVED, AND NOT WITH A FOURTH HEURISTIC. The tempo on these two builds is a STATIC BYTE that the play routine only ever reads, and it is found by asking the CONSUMER rather than hunting for a producer -- which is what the verify said the answer would take. (A) THE MECHANISM, READ OFF THE INSTRUCTIONS THAT IMPLEMENT IT. Every Matt Gray build reloads its per-frame tick counter the same way, and that reload IS what frames-per-tick means: `dec tempo_ctr / bpl skip / lda tempo_slot / sta tempo_ctr`, with the `sta` naming the very address the `dec` just decremented. Maze_Mania $112E-$1139 is the reference: dec $159C / bpl / lda $159A / sta $159C. Requiring the sta and dec to name the SAME address is what makes this a reload rather than any two nearby memory ops. (B) ON A TABLE BUILD THE SLOT IS RAM; ON THESE TWO IT IS DATA. Hyperion_2's slot $B2BA is written at $AF1E by the `lda tune_tempo,y` the table scan finds. Pogo_Stick_Olympics' slot $140E and Warriors' $240E are written by NOTHING -- the only xref to either is a single `lda abs` ($10A4 and $20A4). So their value is baked into the image, and it is 3 on both. (C) CROSS-VALIDATED AGAINST FILES WHOSE ANSWER IS ALREADY KNOWN, which is the step the three previous wrong answers skipped. On the table builds the image byte at the slot AGREES with the located tempo table: Hyperion_2 slot byte 4 against a table reading [0,4,5,5,3,5]; Maze_Mania slot byte 5 against [0,5,3,6,6,7]. The idea was therefore tested where it could be falsified before being applied where it could not. (D) THE RESULT MEETS BOTH HALVES OF THE VERIFY EXACTLY. parse_sid over SID/Gray_Matt goes 11/55 -> 13/55, and native_dispatch._probe_mattgray also reads 13/55, so the probe/decode gap the dispatcher carried is now ZERO. Both new files read tempo 3, frames_per_tick 4 -- inside the 2-5 band every other rip reads -- and no decoding file's tempo moved. (E) AND THE NEW DECODES ARE RIGHT FOR A REASON INDEPENDENT OF THE TEMPO. All three added (file, subtune) pairs have ZERO unreachable track references: Pogo sub1 21 refs into 22 patterns, sub2 2 into 22, Warriors sub1 23 into 23. They pass the existing majority-unreachable guard with room rather than squeaking past it. (F) THE STATIC SLOT IS NOT INDEXED BY SUBTUNE, and that mattered: `tempo = byte(tempo_tab + subtune)` would read $140E+1 = $70 on Pogo, a row every 113 frames. A one-byte slot holds one tempo for the whole song, so the locate records a `tune_tempo_static` flag and the song build indexes from 0.

Verified at three independent points in the source rather than taken from the log, which already asserted this. (A) `traces` IS A CACHE, NOT A FEATURE GATE. build_native_song's signature has `traces=None` (bin/build_mon_native_song.py:1658). When it is supplied, `pbtr = traces[2] if len(traces) > 2 else None` (1689). When it is NOT, the else branch computes `pbtr = passband_trace(sid, sub, secs)` (1696) -- the SAME call the caller would have made. The windowed caller builds its 3-tuple as `(F.per_frame(...), filter_trace(...), passband_trace(...))` at 2756-2757, so both routes end at the identical function with the identical arguments. (B) THE SINGLE-FILE CALL IS LINE 2799, `build_native_song(m, sid, sub, idx_map, instr_rows)` with no `traces=`, so it takes the else branch and traces the passband itself. It is not building 'without a passband trace'; it is building without a CACHED one, which costs time and changes nothing. (C) AND THE TWO SPANS ARE THE SAME EXPRESSION, checked because a cache that computes its argument differently would not be a pure cache. Both compute `span = m.tick_to_frame(max(sum(ev.dur for ev in m.voices[v]) for v in range(3)))` then `secs = span // 50 + 4`. The ONLY difference is that the windowed path adds `getattr(m, 'onset_delay', 0)` at 2753. (D) AND THAT DELTA IS ZERO FOR EVERY MoN ENGINE BUT ONE. mon_parser.py:139 defines onset_delay as `2 if ol_mode == 'supremacy' else 0`, with the docstring 'the Hawkeye/Cybernoid engine validated at 0'. So for every non-Supremacy tune the two paths compute a byte-identical span, secs and therefore trace; for Supremacy the span differs by 2 frames, which changes `span // 50 + 4` only when those 2 frames cross a multiple of 50, and pbtr is read through `min(onset + k, len(pbtr) - 1)` (1047) so a shorter trace clamps rather than misreads. (E) SO THERE IS NOTHING TO FIX, and the record that opened this task said so from the other direction: 'the previous cycle's hoist was a no-op ... SHOULD BE CLOSED AS A FALSE PREMISE rather than fixed'. That is now confirmed against the source rather than inherited.

head: 57f6ca3
evidence: SCOPED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THIS TASK MUST NOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN -- its premise is FALSE, and I confirmed that by re-measuring rather than by reading the record that says so. (A) WHAT THIS TASK WAS FOR. Its parent, detect-filter-drives-blind-to-mode-only-changes, went through three cycles: partial (stopped on an undeclared path), partial (searched 60 files across two corpora at -t20 and found ZERO events the detector is blind to, and proposed closing this as unexercised on the HardTrack field-5-bit-4 precedent), then DONE -- which widened the search and found one. So this task exists to PIN an absence with a test named for it, and the absence is not there. (B) THE BLINDNESS IS STRUCTURAL, CONFIRMED AT THE LINE. detect_filter_drives keys on `abs(ftr[f][0] - ftr[f - 1][0]) >= FILT_FAST` (bin/build_mon_native_song.py:966, again at :982) with FILT_FAST = 0x40 at :897. `ftr[f][0]` is the 11-bit cutoff; the row is a (cutoff, $D417) 2-tuple and the passband lives in $D418, carried separately as pbtr. So a filter event signalled by $D418 alone cannot reach the detector by SIGNATURE. (The parent's line citations had drifted -- it names filter_trace at 744, which is now unrelated code -- so this was re-located rather than followed.) (C) AND THE CORPUS DOES EXERCISE IT. Re-measured SID/Fun_Fun/Byte_Bite.sid with my own implementation of the windowed criterion (a passband change at f with NO |dcutoff| >= FILT_FAST anywhere in [f-8, f+8]), built on fidelity_common.siddump_frames_full whose per-frame globals carry cutoff, filtctl and volmode together: 992 passband changes over 3000 frames, of which 986 are blind. That is the parent's number to the unit, reached independently. (D) AND IT IS NOT A DIGI ARTEFACT, which is the confound that has burned this repo before ($D418's low nibble is the digi carrier, and a sample sweep moves bits 4-6 as a side effect). The volume nibble changes 194 times against 992 passband changes -- it moves, but nowhere near often enough to explain them. The passband toggles between exactly two values (0 and 1, off and low-pass) on a period-6 grid: blind frames 25, 26, 31, 32, 37, 38, 43, 44. Meanwhile the file sweeps cutoff normally -- 16 distinct cutoff values and 15 fast jumps -- so it is not a file that simply never filters. (E) SO WRITING THIS TASK'S TEST WOULD PIN A DISPROVED CLAIM. A test named `test_passband_blindness_is_not_exercised_by_this_corpus` would assert something one file in this repo falsifies, and it would pass only because the corpus scan behind it was too narrow.

evidence: WIRED, AND PROVEN TO FIRE -- which is the part that matters, because a screen that never speaks is indistinguishable from the dead code it replaced. (C) IT NEEDED A NEW RENDERER, AND I PUT IT SOMEWHERE REUSABLE. fidelity_common.artifact_trace() wraps a built .sf2 as a PSID and siddumps it. Deliberate difference from pyscript/passband_check.py's equivalent: the probe goes to a TEMPDIR, not beside the artifact. passband_check writes out/<player>/_passband_probe_<stem>.sid and removes it in a finally whose os.remove is wrapped in `except OSError: pass`, so a kill mid-siddump strands a .sid inside a corpus directory -- and it forces any caller to hold write access to out/. A tempdir cannot litter the corpus and needs no such access, which is why this task could wire the screen without declaring out/mon at all. (D) THE FIRST WIRING WAS SILENTLY DEAD AND MY OWN GUARD CAUGHT IT. I passed the builder's existing traces[0], which is mon_fidelity.per_frame output -- and trace_voice_bundles REFUSES that shape by design, raising 'needs siddump_frames_full() output; siddump_per_frame() drops adsr and would silently measure a weaker key'. (E) AND THE SLICE IS LOAD-BEARING, not a detail. Part N covers frames [t0,t1) of the song but its artifact renders from frame 0, so comparing the whole original against a later part's render lines up two different pieces of music. Everything after part 1 would false-alarm. My first cost probe compared a full trace against part01 and looked fine precisely because part01 starts at 0 -- the one part where the bug is invisible.

SID/Fun_Fun holds 20 .sid but only Delirious_9_tune_1 and Road_of_Excess_end decode to a ROMUZAK sound bank -- and they share it BYTE FOR BYTE (sound table $36F6, drum table $2D60, identical contents). (B) bit5 FILTER IS UNEXERCISED: set on 0 of 64 sounds. That is exactly the branch the verify says to close with a measured count rather than model blind, and it is now closed -- the TODO is replaced with the count, the file names and the reasoning, and pinned by a test. Voice 2 selects a drum sound 363 times in Delirious_9 and 560 in Road_of_Excess; voice 1 24 and 14; voice 0 never. This is the percussion voice of both songs. (D) THE DRUM TABLE IS LOCATED AND ITS SHAPE IS READ: $2D60 holds EIGHT little-endian pointers ($2D7D $2D94 $2DA5 $2DB0 $2D70 $2DBB $2DD2 $2DEF) with data starting immediately after them at $2D70 in 4-byte rows; the first two are `81 C0 11 04` and `81 C0 11 02`, differing only in the last byte. So a default SDI build -- which really runs at FILT_LEAD=64 -- stamps the same empty string as a build with no flags at all. Two artifacts with different effective flags are indistinguishable by provenance, which is precisely the confound class this task exists to remove. (C) THE SIX CONFOUNDED FILES ARE THE SIX LONGEST, which explains the -j16 timeouts mechanically. evidence: SCOPED, AND THE ANOMALY METRIC IN THE OPENING RECORD IS THE WRONG ONE -- it flags long songs, not bad splits. Nothing written. (A) THE OPENING RECORD LISTS SIX FILES BY PART COUNT: End_94 1190, GT_Groove 402, L-Forza_long_edit 174, Stort_Plaster 137, L-Forza_Remix 127, Tanks_3000 69, 'with implausible part counts driven by very short per-part windows'. Part COUNT and window TIGHTNESS are different quantities, and separating them changes the population. (B) MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE CORPUS: 278 songs in out/sdi carry both parts and .span sidecars. Seconds of music per part -- span end divided by part count -- has a MEDIAN of 22.5 and a smooth tail: 58 songs below 10 s/part, 15 below 5. It is a continuum, not a cliff, so 'six anomalies' understates it by an order of magnitude if tightness is the criterion. (C) AND LENGTH DOES NOT DRIVE IT. Correlation between song span and seconds-per-part is -0.011 over n=278 -- essentially zero. By length bucket the median s/part is flat: 0-60s -> 17.0, 60-150s -> 25.9, 150-400s -> 24.9, 400-1000s -> 21.6, 1000s+ -> 9.5. The tightest song in the 60-150s bucket (2.1 s/part) is as tight as the tightest song over 1000s (2.0). Short songs split just as tightly as long ones. (D) SO HALF THE NAMED LIST IS NOT ANOMALOUS. Tanks_3000 is 69 parts over 1602s = 23.2 s/part, ABOVE the corpus median of 22.5 -- it has many parts because it is long, and its split is entirely ordinary. L-Forza_long_edit (9.0) and L-Forza_Remix (9.5) are below median but inside a band 58 songs share. Only End_94 (2.0), GT_Groove (4.0) and Stort_Plaster (4.3) are genuinely in the tight tail. (E) AND THE COUNTEREXAMPLES THE LIST MISSES ARE THE INTERESTING ONES: 64_Antheme is 37 parts over 76 SECONDS (2.1 s/part) and What_Is_Love 79 parts over 168s (2.1). Neither is long, both split as tightly as End_94, and neither appears in the opening record -- because a part-count filter cannot see them.

head: ff52cb4
evidence: THE VERIFY'S PRESCRIBED GROUND-TRUTH METHOD IS REFUTED WITH A MECHANISM, and it took no GUI at all to do it -- the last cycle's open question ('establish WHAT THE TOP-LEFT ORDERLIST PANEL ACTUALLY SHOWS') is now answered offline. (A) THE PANEL SHOWS A STUB THE CONVERTER WRITES, IDENTICAL ON EVERY FILE. Converting Angular, Cascade and Cycles to SF2 (into the scratchpad, outside the repo) and parsing each with sf2_viewer_core.SF2Parser, the SF2-level orderlist is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three -- a0 00 fe ff ff... -- unpacking to track0 {transpose $A0, sequence 0}, track1 {$A0, 1}, track2 {$A0, 2}. That is exactly the '0000: 00 01 02' with labels a000/a001/a002 that last cycle's SF2II screenshot showed for BOTH Angular and Cascade. The identical reading was not a fluke of two files; it is structural. (B) THE SAME PARSER READS THE PAYLOAD CORRECTLY, so the SF2 carries both and the editor reads the wrong one. SF2Parser.laxity_orderlists on the SAME three artifacts is file-SPECIFIC and reproduces the locate exactly: Angular 87 01 / 93 02 / 87 05, Cascade 85 07 / 85 09 / 91 05, Cycles 93 01 / 87 0C / 87 02 -- i.e. 01/02/05, 07/09/05, 01/0C/02, matching last cycle's predictions from locate_seq_ptr_table + read_orderlist_numbers read off the SID. So the located orderlists survive the round-trip into the SF2 and can be read back; the editor panel just is not the thing reading them. The stub is 1-2 positions long against Angular's 14 sequences, which is what a stub looks like: the Laxity driver plays from the embedded NP21 payload, so the emitted SF2 needs only enough Driver-11-shaped orderlist for the editor to open the file. (C) AND THE STUB CAN NEVER ACCIDENTALLY AGREE. Across all 14 files the locate accepts, the native first entries are 01 02 05 / 08 02 01 / 0E 00 0A / 01 03 05 / 01 03 06 / 07 09 05 / 01 02 17 / 01 02 03 / 01 0C 02 / 05 02 05 / 01 02 03 / 01 05 07 / 07 08 02 / 01 11 09 -- ZERO of 14 are 00 01 02. A panel showing the stub therefore disagrees with every file by construction, INCLUDING Angular, whose 01/02/05 is independently proven. An 'agreement' is impossible and a 'disagreement' is worthless, which is precisely why the method discriminated nothing last cycle. (D) THE OBVIOUS FALLBACK IS ALSO DEAD, and its own control killed it. I built a decoder that expands each voice's located orderlist into a note stream and compares its INTERVAL shape against siddump note onsets. Run on the three CONFIRMED files first, it scored 0 of 39 agreeing intervals on every voice. The reason is visible in the dump: Angular's onsets are B-7 (semitone 95, top of the table) on all three voices -- the instrument's arpeggio and wave program own the sounded pitch, not the sequencer. A tool that fails on the files whose answer is known cannot be pointed at the eleven whose answer is not. (E) WRITTEN UP AND PINNED. docs/players/LAXITY.md +49 records the stub, the three-file table, the 0-of-14 count and both refutations; pyscript/test_laxity_parser.py +88 adds two tests -- that no real orderlist starts 00/01/02 (behind a >=10-file positive control) and that Angular's reads exactly 01/02/05.

With BM.FILT_LEAD = 64 (the SDI default, not the 4 the source comment beside it assumes) the credit window is [-1, +64] and the drive is credited. What is lost is the capture: the program is captured FROM the onset, and the attack peak is at onset-1. (C) MEASURED, NOT REASONED, AND THE PICTURE IS UNAMBIGUOUS. Funk_Facet's routed voice is 0. Raw cutoff around onset 97: frames 87-95 flat at 256, frame 96 jumps to 1920 (+1664), frame 97 -- THE ONSET -- is already 1672 and decaying -248/frame to 432 by 102. Onset 121 is identical in shape: frame 120 = 1920, onset 121 = 1632, then -288/frame. The single brightest frame of the note is always the frame BEFORE the gate rise, so filter_program_for's SET row is the first DECAY value and the attack transient is dropped. (D) HOW OFTEN, over all 304 routed onsets: the attack peak lands BEFORE the onset on 152, ON the onset on ZERO, and after/flat on 152. The 152/152 split is not noise -- the song alternates two note types, one opening with a pre-onset spike and one with a +80/frame rise, and it is exactly the spiked half that loses its peak. Median cutoff lost is 288 of a 2047 full scale (14%), and it is 288 on essentially every one of them. (E) AND IT IS NOT A FUNK_FACET QUIRK. Arabia (routed voice 2, the other file FILT_LEAD was raised for) shows the same shape on 218 of 356 onsets, again ZERO with the peak at the onset -- though its median loss is only 8 with a 848 tail, so the severity is very uneven. Whatever the anchor fix is, it is at least a two-file question and probably a shared-builder one.

Both are now true of pyscript/sdi_native_sweep.py; the multi-hour detached relaunch is what remains. (A) THE 2026-08-20 DEATH WAS UNATTRIBUTABLE FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, and fixing one would have left the other. First, the ONLY record was the launcher's stdout redirect -- and a redirect captures nothing a dying process never manages to print, which is exactly why the log froze at three banner lines. Second, that log, the result JSON and the START_EPOCH file all lived in a session scratchpad (70d2da07-d9c4-4571-9fb9-b13eede4d75c) that was emptied on 2026-08-29, so even the evidence that DID exist is gone. I confirmed that directory is empty this cycle. (B) THE SWEEP NOW KEEPS ITS OWN JOURNAL. `<--json>.journal`, rewritten after EVERY file with state/started/pid/done/total/built/last_file, and closed by an atexit hook that stamps how the run ended. A journal still reading `running` when the process goes down is rewritten to `died` with 'process exited while the sweep was still running' -- the line the 2026-08-20 death did not leave. It is derived from --json rather than given its own flag, deliberately: a separate flag is a separate thing to forget, and it lands beside the result instead of in a temp directory, which is the specific way the last evidence was lost. write_journal() is atomic (tmp + os.replace) and swallows every exception -- the black box must never become the cause. (C) AND A 0-FILE SWEEP IS NO LONGER REPORTABLE AS A COMPLETED ONE. main() previously wrote a well-formed result JSON and returned 0 whatever the built count was; the only tell was a zero buried in the summary. It now writes `complete: true|false` INTO the file and returns 1 when nothing was built, so a shell chain and a later reader each see the failure without interpreting a count. Verified by running the real CLI: exit code 1, complete=False, journal state `no-files-built`. (D) MY OWN CHANGE HAD A BUG AND ITS POSITIVE CONTROL CAUGHT IT. main() set the terminal journal state but only the atexit hook wrote it, so the file on disk still read `running` until interpreter shutdown -- a watchdog or a human checking a detached job in that window would see a finished run as live. Fixed by writing at the end of main() too. A SECOND bug surfaced the same way: _JOURNAL is module state, so a second main() in one process reported the FIRST run's built count against the second run's total (built=8, total=1). Every counter is now reset when the journal is armed. (E) 9 new tests in pyscript/test_sdi_native_sweep.py (12 -> 28 passing with its two sibling sweep test files and the pyflakes guard). evidence: SCOPED, AND THE TITLE UNDERSTATES IT TWICE: $0D7E is not a special load, it is 99.8% of every SF2 in the tree; and $0903 does not have one wrong reading, it has THREE incompatible ones, none of which locates sequences. Nothing written. (A) '$0903 IS BELOW THE LOAD ADDRESS' IS NOT A $0D7E QUIRK -- IT IS UNIVERSAL. Scanned every .sf2 under out/, SF2/ and bin/music/: 8,769 files, and ZERO load at or below $0903. Load addresses are $0D7E on 8,754, $0DFE on 14, $0C00 on 1. So `0x0903 - load_addr` is negative on the ENTIRE corpus, not on one file. This widens sf2_player_parser's own comment, which says '364 of 364 out/*.sf2', by a factor of 24. (B) THREE READINGS OF THE SAME NUMBER LIVE IN THE TREE, and each is in a different frame of reference: sidm2/sf2_player_parser.py:314 treats it as an ABSOLUTE address (`0x0903 - load_addr + 2`); sidm2/sf2_packer.py:219 treats it as an offset FROM THE DRIVER TOP (`self.driver_top + SEQUENCE_TABLE_OFFSET`, driver_top = $1000, so $1903); sidm2/galway_table_injector.py:44 treats it as a BARE file offset (`'sequences': 0x0903`). CLAUDE.md:148 states it as `SEQ=0x0903` with no frame at all, which is how three readings can each look like they are following the documentation. (C) AND NONE OF THE THREE LANDS ON THE REAL DATA. In SF2II's own bin/music/Driver 11 Test - Arpeggio.sf2 the sequences are at raw 0x19AE = address $272A = load + $19AC, and they read `c1 a0 80 30 30 00 c2 81 30 30 c3 80` -- the packed grammar, cleanly. The three candidate offsets give: absolute -> raw -1145 (outside, now refused); driver-top -> raw 0x0B87 = `00 0f 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`; bare -> raw 0x0905 = `82 6e 68 6e 88 af eb 39 9c 13`. Neither of the two in-range candidates is a sequence stream. (D) WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING, because it would be the easy over-read: the packer is NOT shown to be broken. It WRITES files rather than reading foreign ones, its $1903 lands on plausible table data in our own SF2s (`11 1a 1b 1b f2 ...` in Angular), and its sibling constant already carries a measured correction (`WAVE_TABLE_OFFSET = 0x09db  # Fixed: was 0x0B03 (296 bytes too high)`), so that frame has been validated against something. The proven defect is sf2_player_parser's absolute reading, which fails on 8,769 of 8,769 files. (E) AND OUR OWN FILES DO NOT SHARE THE EDITOR'S LAYOUT EITHER: at raw 0x19AE, Angular holds `00 08 08 00 ...` and Balance holds ASCII (`ut.Legato.Re`). So $19AC is that ONE file's offset, not a better constant. The conclusion is the same one 73780fa reached for Laxity: locate the region, never index to a constant.

head: ff52cb4
evidence: THE PACKED DECODER IS IN, AND THE VERIFY'S TEST EXISTS: a real SF2's sequence now decodes to the SAME events sf2_viewer_core.unpack_sequence produces, asserted event-for-event. (A) WHAT WAS REPLACED. sf2_player_parser._extract_sequences_from_sf2 walked the sequence region as fixed 3-byte (instrument, command, note) groups, `offset += 3`, terminating on note == $7F. That is wrong about the format. New module function `unpack_packed_sequence(data, offset) -> ([SequenceEvent], next_offset)` implements the real grammar -- $C0-$FF command, $A0-$BF instrument, $80-$9F duration (bits 0-3 ticks, bit 4 tie), $00-$7E note, $7F end, $E1 skipped as offset-table padding -- with every field OPTIONAL and in that order, so a row is one to four bytes. 84 added, 19 removed. (B) THE DURATION FIELD WAS NOT ADDED, AND THAT IS THE FIX RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL. The task's title asks for a duration on SequenceEvent, and the previous cycle stopped because sidm2/models.py is not in this task's touches. It does not need to be: the editor's own unpacker EXPANDS a duration of N into N following sustain rows ($7E, or $00 when the note is a gate-off), so expanding here yields the same stream instead of a differently-shaped one every consumer would have to learn about. models.py keeps its three fields and the undeclared-path problem dissolves. (C) THE TEST IS AN EQUIVALENCE, NOT A HAND-WRITTEN EXPECTATION, which is what makes it evidence. The reference bytes are verbatim from SF2 II's own bin/music/Driver 11 Test - Arpeggio.sf2 at raw 0x19AE -- a file no analysis of ours produced -- and the assertion is that this decoder and unpack_sequence (documented from the editor source, predating this change) produce identical (instrument, command, note) triples. A hand-written expectation would just be this decoder's output copied down and would pass for any grammar I happened to write. (D) WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, so the agreement is not a property of the input: read as fixed triples the same bytes yield ZERO legal instrument bytes and a different event count. If that ever stops being true the premise of the change needs re-checking, and the test says so. (E) 4 -> 9 tests in pyscript/test_sf2_player_parser.py; 47 pass across it plus test_driver11_section_injectors.py, test_sf2_viewer_core.py and the pyflakes guard.

head: ff52cb4
evidence: ALL THREE STUBS DESCRIBE A UI SF2 II DOES NOT HAVE, so the verify -- 'each of the three actions is confirmed by a screenshot of the running editor' -- is UNSATISFIABLE, and not because the automation is hard. Measured against bin/config.ini, the editor's OWN key map, 105 `Key.*` bindings. (A) VOLUME: ZERO of the 105 bindings mention volume or gain. The only volume control anywhere in the config is `Sound.Output.Gain = 1.0`, read at STARTUP. There is no settings menu to open and no slider to drag, so the old TODO ('open settings/volume menu, adjust slider, confirm') describes something that does not exist. Changing the gain means editing config.ini and RESTARTING -- a different operation with a different signature (a float gain, not this method's 0-100 int). (B) LOOP: AND Ctrl+L IS AN ACTIVE TRAP. The old TODO guessed 'Menu: View -> Loop Playback' or 'Ctrl+L or similar'. Ctrl+L IS bound -- to `Key.ScreenEdit.SetOrderlistLoopPointAll`, with `@l:shift:control` bound to `Key.Track.SetOrderlistLoopPoint`. Those set the orderlist LOOP POINT: they EDIT THE SONG, permanently. An implementation taking the obvious guess would silently rewrite the user's music while reporting success. The nearest playback-loop concept, `Playback.StopEmulationIfDriverStops`, is also a startup setting. (C) POSITION: no seek binding exists. What exists is PLAY FROM a position -- Play @f1, PlayFromMarker @f2, PlayFromLast @f2:shift, PlayFromCursor @f2:control. SF2 II is a tracker, not a media player; there is no slider and no field. The nearest real behaviour (move the cursor, Ctrl+F2) STARTS PLAYBACK rather than seeking, so it does not satisfy set_position's contract. (D) SO NOTHING WAS IMPLEMENTED AND THAT IS THE RESULT. All three still return False; what changed is that the three misleading TODOs are replaced by the measurement, with the config lines quoted in place (sidm2/sf2_editor_automation.py +40/-14), and four tests pin it (pyscript/test_editor_automation.py +90). (E) THE EDITOR WAS NEVER LAUNCHED, deliberately: config.ini ENUMERATES every binding, which is stronger evidence for an ABSENT control than a screenshot of one place it is not. The desktop singleton was free before and after; no SIDFactoryII.exe process was started.

The defect is upstream: ch_seq_ptr is the player's RUNTIME current-sequence pointer, and in an SF2-wrapped payload it sits at a different address holding values that are not this song's orderlists. (D) THREE RESIDUALS, THREE MECHANISMS, none of them the single cause the task's title assumes: Stinsens -- the pointer-table locate finds ZERO candidates, so it falls to the same heuristic by a different route; Dreamy -- the locate SUCCEEDS and the cross-check declines it, as above; Blue -- locates cleanly and its gap is a legitimate shape difference (22 sequences vs 1) that no fix can close. A value whose two bytes are equal and increment together is a TABLE INDEX landing in $D400/$D401, not a pitch. (E) SO: from frame 586 our voice 1 runs a wave/arp program the original does not, and its table index leaks into the frequency pair. Written into docs/players/LAXITY.md (+117) with the register table, the run list, both tells, and an explicit instruction not to quote 98.73% as inaudible.

evidence: THE VERIFY PASSES ON BOTH CLAUSES, and the fix is the CONSUMER approach the previous partial named as the next place to look -- it is implemented and committed at HEAD as mattgray_parser._static_tempo_slot(), so this cycle's work was to confirm it is RIGHT rather than merely green. Nothing written. (A) BOTH FILES DECODE WITH A TEMPO IN THE 2-5 RANGE: Pogo_Stick_Olympics tempo=3 fpt=4, Warriors tempo=3 fpt=4. (B) PROBE AND DECODE ARE BOTH 13/55, and both lists contain exactly these two names -- the 11/55 -> 13/55 the verify asks for, with the delta being the two files in question rather than any other pair. (C) 'IN THE 2-5 RANGE' IS THE WEAK TEST THAT PRODUCED THE TWO RECORDED WRONG ANSWERS, so I verified STRUCTURALLY instead: disassembled the reload idiom out of each image and read the byte it loads. Pogo_Stick_Olympics has exactly ONE `dec/branch/lda/sta` reload, at $109F: `dec $1410 / bpl / lda $140E / sta $1410`, and image[$140E] = 3, so frames-per-tick is 4. Warriors has exactly one, at $209F: `dec $2410 / bpl / lda $240E / sta $2410`, image[$240E] = 3, fpt 4. Both agree with the decode, and the value is read off the instruction that IMPLEMENTS frames-per-tick rather than inferred from a table's position -- which is why this is not a fourth heuristic. (D) AND IT AGREES WITH AN INDEPENDENT ANSWER ON THE CONTROLS, which is the part that makes it evidence rather than self-consistency. On the table builds the tempo comes from a located TABLE, so the reload slot is a second, unrelated route to the same number: Hyperion_2's idiom loads $B2BA whose image byte is 4, and its table-derived tempo is 4; Maze_Mania's second idiom loads $159A whose byte is 5, and its table-derived tempo is 5. Two mechanisms, same answer, twice. (E) A STRUCTURAL FACT THAT EXPLAINS WHY THESE TWO FAILED TOGETHER: they are the SAME BUILD RELOCATED BY $1000. Every address in the idiom is offset by exactly that -- $109F/$209F, $1410/$2410, $140E/$240E. They were never two independent mysteries; they are one player at two load addresses, which is also why all three earlier heuristics failed on both rather than on one. (F) MAZE_MANIA CARRIES A DECOY and it justifies the locator's strictness: it has TWO reload idioms, and the first loads $1001 whose byte is 0 (fpt 1, absurd). The locator's rule that no code site may write the slot is what discards it.

evidence: THIRD CYCLE. THE FIRST OF THE TWO NAMED BLOCKERS IS NOW CLOSED AS AN ENGINEERING QUESTION, measured, and the answer is two orders of magnitude rather than a tuning. Nothing written. (A) THE PRIOR CYCLE LEFT EXACTLY THIS. Its blocker (1) was 'COST: 7.3x on the suite (99.6s -> 726.9s). The widened scan tries ~60 candidate lengths per offset where the exact path's modulo-128 arithmetic tries about one; the fix is to derive a cheap necessary condition on `cand` from the shifted case before building any pointer list, not to accept the brute force.' That is the condition I derived and measured. (B) MY FIRST IDEA WAS WRONG AND READING THE CODE KILLED IT, which is worth recording because it would have been a plausible paragraph. I reasoned that ptrs[0] is fixed once tbl is fixed, so cand <= (ptrs[0]-tbl)/2 bounds the search in O(1). FALSE: the table is SPLIT lo/hi -- sf2_viewer_core.py:1512 reads `data[off+i] | (data[off+cand+i] << 8)`, so entry 0's HIGH byte is at off+cand and moves with the candidate. ptrs[0] is not fixed. (C) BUT THE SAME LAYOUT HANDS OVER THE REAL BOUND: entry 0 costs exactly TWO byte reads, data[off] and data[off+cand], for any cand. So compute p0 = data[off] | (data[off+cand] << 8), then shift = p0 - tbl - 2*cand, and reject unless 0 <= shift <= SHIFT_MAX and p0 is in the image -- all before building the cand-length pointer list. (D) IT IS A NECESSARY CONDITION, NOT A HEURISTIC, and that is the part that makes it safe to ship. The cheap test computes the SAME ptrs[0] the full path computes, from the same two bytes, so it can only reject candidates the full check would also reject. There is no tolerance to tune and no file it can silently lose. (E) MEASURED ON THE FOUR NAMED FILES, prototyped in the scratchpad against the real payloads. Pointer lists built, brute force vs cheap: Stinsens 776,957 -> 1,572 (494x fewer, 20.8x faster); Angular 479,826 -> 1,882 (255x, 20.8x); Blue 381,616 -> 2,213 (172x, 20.0x); Dreamy 342,149 -> 2,068 (165x, 17.5x). head: ff52cb4
evidence: THE QUESTION THE PREVIOUS RECORD SAID MUST BE SETTLED FIRST IS SETTLED, and it settles AGAINST that record's own guess -- which changes which fix is correct. Nothing written. (A) WHAT IT ASKED. It observed that the frequency-table size distribution is '0 or 96 with nothing between, which is not what a merely-misplaced constant usually looks like', inferred 'the extractor is probably REFUSING (returning empty) rather than reading garbage, which would mean the honest failure is already there and only the CLAMP is hiding it', and said the distinction 'decides whether the fix is find the table or stop clamping and refuse loudly, and it should be settled by reading _extract_frequency_table before either is written'. (B) THE CODE SETTLES IT OUTRIGHT. sidm2/sequence_translator.py:77-105 computes freq_offset = LAXITY_FREQ_TABLE_ADDR - 0x1000 = $0835, then offset = freq_addr - load_addr, which reduces to that same constant because the load address CANCELS -- the 'non-standard load address' handling in its docstring is a no-op. The ONLY path returning [] is `offset + 192 > len(c64_data)`: a file too SHORT. There is no validity check on the bytes. It never refuses a bad table; it reads 96 entries from $0835 whatever is there. (C) AND THE CORPUS CONFIRMS BOTH HALVES. Over 303 Laxity SIDs: 61 are shorter than 2,293 bytes and get [], 242 return 96 entries. So the 0-or-96 distribution is FILE LENGTH, not refusal. (D) OF THOSE 242, THE CONSTANT READS GARBAGE ON 240. Scoring by the one property a frequency table cannot fake -- f[i+12] within 2% of 2*f[i], an octave doubling -- only 2 files score >=90%: ANGULAR and OMNIPHUNK, both 97.6%. 224 score below 90%, and 16 read all zeros. Sample garbage: 1983_Sauna_Tango f[0]=33024 f[95]=8321, which DESCENDS. (E) AND ZERO OF 242 ARE STRICTLY ASCENDING, which a real 96-semitone table must be. So the constant is wrong even on the two files where it starts in the right place -- the 96-entry window overruns the table's end there too. (F) SO THE FIX IS 'FIND THE TABLE', NOT 'REFUSE LOUDLY'. The honest failure is NOT already present: removing the clamp alone would ship wrong pitches loudly instead of exposing an existing refusal, because there is no refusal to expose.

  offset      = freq_addr - load_addr                # load_addr CANCELS -> $0835
  if offset < 0 or offset + 192 > len(c64_data): return []   # SHORT FILE only

Here the FREQUENCY table constant reads a real table on 2 of 242 -- Angular and Omniphunk.
